title: Basic Semiconductor Devices

notes.heading: 1. Band Gap, Doping, Mass-Action Law & Drift Mobility
notes.proseLatex: Room-temperature band gaps are $E_g \approx 0.72\text{ eV}$ ($\text{Ge}$) and $1.12\text{ eV}$ ($\text{Si}$), giving semiconductors a NEGATIVE temperature coefficient of resistance! Pentavalent Group-15 donors ($\text{P, As, Sb}$) create $n$-type (electrons majority, immobile positive donor ions — the crystal as a whole remains ELECTRICALLY NEUTRAL!), while trivalent Group-13 acceptors ($\text{B, Al, Ga, In}$) create $p$-type. At thermal equilibrium, mass-action law $n\cdot p = n_i^2$ holds in BOTH intrinsic and doped semiconductors, with conductivity $\sigma = q(n\mu_n + p\mu_p)$.

keyFormulas.label: Mass-Action Law & Drift Conductivity
keyFormulas.latex: $n\cdot p = n_i^2,\qquad \sigma = q(n\mu_n + p\mu_p),\qquad V_T = \frac{kT}{q} \approx 26\text{ mV at }300\text{ K}$
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Compute minority carrier concentration from n_i^2 / N_D and semiconductor conductivity.

examples.problemLatex: Silicon ($n_i = 1.5\times 10^{10}\text{ cm}^{-3}$) is doped with $N_D = 4.5\times 10^{15}\text{ cm}^{-3}$ phosphorus atoms. Find equilibrium hole concentration $p_0$.

notes.heading: 2. p-n Junction, Zener Voltage Regulator & Rectifier Parameters
notes.proseLatex: Cut-in barrier voltage is $\sim 0.7\text{ V}$ ($\text{Si}$) and $\sim 0.3\text{ V}$ ($\text{Ge}$), decreasing by $\sim 2\text{ mV}/^\circ\text{C}$ as temperature rises. Forward bias narrows the depletion layer; reverse bias widens it (varactor capacitance $C_j \downarrow$). Heavily doped Zener diodes operate in REVERSE breakdown as shunt voltage regulators! Rectifier comparison: Half-Wave ($\eta_{\max} = 40.6\%,\; \text{RF} = 1.21,\; f_{\text{ripple}} = f$); Centre-Tap Full-Wave ($\eta_{\max} = 81.2\%,\; \text{RF} = 0.482,\; f_{\text{ripple}} = 2f,\; \text{PIV} = 2V_m$); Bridge Full-Wave ($\eta_{\max} = 81.2\%,\; \text{PIV} = V_m$!).

keyFormulas.label: Half-Wave vs Centre-Tap vs Bridge Rectifier Benchmarks
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Recall efficiency, ripple factor, ripple frequency, and PIV of HWR/CT-FWR/Bridge.

notes.heading: 3. BJT (α, β), MOSFET & CMOS Low-Power Logic
notes.proseLatex: A BJT is a bipolar CURRENT-controlled device ($I_E = I_B + I_C$); in the ACTIVE region (E-B forward, C-B reverse) it amplifies with $\beta = \frac{I_C}{I_B} = \frac{\alpha}{1 - \alpha}$ ($\alpha = \frac{\beta}{\beta + 1} < 1$), whereas cutoff (both reverse) + saturation (both forward) act as digital switches. A MOSFET is a unipolar VOLTAGE-controlled majority-carrier device with practically infinite gate input impedance ($I_G \approx 0$). Complementary MOS (CMOS) pairs a pull-up PMOS with a pull-down NMOS, giving NEAR-ZERO static power dissipation and full rail-to-rail noise margins!

keyFormulas.label: BJT Current Gains & Active Biasing Rule
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Convert alpha <-> beta, check BJT region of operation, and contrast BJT vs MOSFET/CMOS.

examples.problemLatex: A transistor has common-base current gain $\alpha = 0.98$ and base current $I_B = 50\,\mu\text{A}$. Find $\beta$ and emitter current $I_E$.

wbjeebTraps: An $n$-type or $p$-type semiconductor crystal is ELECTRICALLY NEUTRAL overall — 'n-type' refers to majority mobile carriers, NOT net negative charge!
PIV trap: Centre-Tapped full-wave rectifier requires diode $\text{PIV} = 2V_m$, whereas a $4$-diode Bridge rectifier needs only $\text{PIV} = V_m$!
Common-Emitter (CE) amplifier introduces $180^\circ$ phase inversion between base input and collector output; Common-Collector (emitter follower) and Common-Base have $0^\circ$ phase shift.
